title: volatile is for things that change behind your back
body: A flag set inside an ISR and polled in main() must be volatile, or the compiler may read it once and loop forever on a stale copy.

title: IOSET and IOCLR only listen to ones
body: On the LPC2129, writing 1 to a bit in IOSET drives the pin high and IOCLR drives it low. Writing 0 does nothing, so no read-modify-write is needed.

title: Five in a row gets a stuff bit
body: After five identical bits the transmitter inserts one opposite bit so receivers keep their clocks in sync. The receiver strips it back out.

title: MCP9700: 500 mV means 0 °C
body: The sensor outputs 500 mV at 0 °C plus 10 mV per degree, so T = (V − 0.5) / 0.01. Forget the offset and every room is 50 °C.

title: Eight custom glyphs live at 0x40
body: An HD44780 has 64 bytes of CGRAM: eight 5×8 characters. Set address 0x40, write eight rows per glyph, then print them as characters 0–7.

title: fork() returns twice
body: Once in the parent with the child's PID, once in the child with 0. Every shell starts its work by checking which one it is.

title: strtok() remembers where it stopped
body: It keeps hidden static state between calls, so it isn't reentrant or thread-safe. In threaded code, use strtok_r().

title: cd has to be a built-in
body: chdir() only changes the calling process's directory. Run it in a child and the change disappears when the child exits.

title: getline() can allocate for you
body: Pass a NULL pointer and a size of 0 and getline() mallocs a buffer big enough for the whole line. You still have to free() it.
